task.title: Build the structures of a formula
task.shortdesc: You write the parts of a formula with the token elements, and you build fractions, roots, scripts, limits, matrices and enclosures by nesting elements.

info.p: The smallest parts of a formula are the tokens. Each token holds text and no other elements:

ul.li: mi is an identifier, such as x, f or sin.
mn is a number.
mo is an operator, a fence or a separator, such as +, ( or ,.
mtext is text that is not math, and ms is a string.

info.p: CSSMedia puts the space around an operator that the language asks for: a binary operator such as + gets space on both sides, and a minus sign at the start of a group is a sign and gets none. To change this, set the form of the operator to prefix, infix or postfix, or set lspace and rspace to lengths.
Use the minus sign − and not a hyphen for a minus.

An mrow puts its children in a row and makes them one part of the formula. Elements that take a fixed number of children, such as mfrac, take one part for each, so you group the tokens of a numerator with an mrow.
mfrac takes a numerator and a denominator. msqrt takes any number of children under a radical sign. mroot takes a base and an index.

fig.title: A square root and a cube root

info.p: The attribute linethickness of mfrac sets the thickness of the bar: a length, or thin, medium or thick. With 0 there is no bar, which is how you write a binomial. The attributes numalign and denomalign align the numerator and the denominator to the left, the center or the right, and bevelled="true" writes the fraction with a slash.

msub, msup and msubsup take a base followed by a subscript, a superscript, or both. mmultiscripts takes a base and pairs of subscripts and superscripts, and the pairs after mprescripts go before the base. An mrow makes a script of several parts. Scripts are smaller than the base.
The attributes subscriptshift and superscriptshift set the least distance by which a script is moved from the baseline of the base.

munder, mover and munderover put a part under or over a base. Use them for the limits of a sum, for an accent and for a brace. An operator in the base, or in the overscript, stretches to the width of the other part. In display style the limits of a big operator, such as a sum, go under and over it. In a line of text they become subscript and superscript, so that the line stays even. Set movablelimits="false" on the operator to keep them under and over, and largeop="false" to keep the operator at the size of the text.

stepxmp.p: The same sum in a line of text is .

info.p: For an accent, set accent="true" on mover, or accentunder="true" on munder. The accent is then set close to the base, at the size of the text. The attribute align aligns the scripts to the left, the center or the right.

fig.title: An accent, an arrow and a brace

info.p: An operator that is a fence stretches to the height of what is between the fences, and it is centered on the math axis, the line of the bar of a fraction. Put the fences and their content in an mrow. Set stretchy="false" on a fence to keep it at the size of the text. The attributes minsize and maxsize set the least and the greatest size of a stretchy operator, and symmetric="false" stops it from being centered on the axis.

The element mfenced writes the fences and the separators for you. Its attributes are open and close, with ( and ) as defaults, and separators, with , as default. The last separator is repeated when there are more children than separators.

mtable holds rows, mtr elements, and each row holds cells, mtd elements. A table is laid out like a CSS table, so the cell and table properties of Tables work on the elements, and a cell can span columns and rows. Put a table between two stretchy brackets to write a matrix:
These attributes of mtable set the look of the table. A list of values, separated by spaces, applies to the rows or columns in turn, and the last value repeats:

ul.li: columnalign is left, center or right, and rowalign is top, center, bottom or baseline. The same attributes on an mtr or an mtd apply to the row or to the cell.
columnspacing and rowspacing are the distances between columns and rows.
columnlines and rowlines are solid, dashed or none, and frame is the line around the table, with framespacing as the space between the frame and the table.
width is the width of the table, columnwidth is the width of each column, and equalrows and equalcolumns give all rows or columns the same size.
align sets the row of the table, top, center, bottom, baseline or axis, that is on the baseline of the line.
columnspan and rowspan on an mtd make a cell cover several columns or rows.

fig.title: Lines, alignment and a spanning cell

info.p: The elements are also styled by CSS. The rule m|mtd { border: 1pt solid black; } draws a line around each cell.

mspace is an empty space of the width, height and depth you give. mpadded changes the size of its content: width, height and depth set the size of its box, lspace moves the content from the start of the box, and voffset raises or lowers it. mphantom takes the room of its content and shows nothing.
menclose draws lines around its content. The attribute notation holds the names of the notations, separated by spaces. A notation that is not in the list draws nothing. These are the names:

ul.li: box, roundedbox and circle enclose the content.
left, right, top, bottom, actuarial, madruwb, phasorangle and longdiv draw lines on some sides.
radical draws a radical sign.
updiagonalstrike, downdiagonalstrike, verticalstrike and horizontalstrike strike the content out.

uparrow, downarrow, leftarrow, rightarrow, updownarrow, leftrightarrow, northeastarrow, northwestarrow, southeastarrow, southwestarrow, northwestsoutheastarrow and northeastsouthwestarrow draw arrows.

info.p: For elementary arithmetic, mstack aligns numbers in columns, as you write them on paper. Its children are rows:

ul.li: msrow is a row of digits. A number in it, such as <mn>199.5</mn>, is split into its digits, and each digit takes a column. Any other child, such as the + of an addition, takes one column.
msline is a horizontal line over the width of the stack.
mscarries is a row of carries over the row that follows it, one child for each column. A child that is <none/>, or an empty mrow, is a column without a carry.
msgroup groups rows that share a position.

info.p: A child of mstack that is none of these is a row of its own, as if it were inside an msrow.
These attributes of mstack set the alignment of the columns. mstyle and math can set them for all the stacks they hold:

ul.li: stackalign chooses the column on which the rows are aligned: decimalpoint (the default), left, center or right. With decimalpoint, a row is aligned on its decimal point, or on the right of its first number when it has none. The attribute decimalcharacter is the character of the decimal point, . by default.
charalign places a digit that is narrower than its column at the left, the center or the right of the column, which is the default.
charspacing is a length: the space between columns. Without it, CSSMedia spaces the columns so that carries that are wider than a digit do not overlap.

align is the row of the stack that is on the baseline of the line: baseline, which is the default, center, axis, top or bottom, and after a space the number of a row, counted from the bottom when it is negative. center and baseline put the middle of the stack on the baseline.

info.p: These attributes work on the rows:

ul.li: position, on msrow, msgroup, mscarries and msline, is an integer number of columns by which the row, or the rows of the group, are moved to the left.
shift, on msgroup, is an integer number of columns by which each row after the first of the group is moved from the row before it. The rows of a long division use it to step to the left.
location, on mscarries and on mscarry, puts a carry at a point of the compass around its digit: n (the default), ne, e, se, s, sw, w or nw.

crossout, on mscarries and on mscarry, is a list of updiagonalstrike, downdiagonalstrike, verticalstrike and horizontalstrike, or none. The lines strike out the digit under the carry, as in a subtraction that borrows. An mscarry holds one carry and overrides the attributes of its mscarries.

length, on msline, is the number of columns that the line covers, ending at the alignment column. Without it, the line covers the stack. leftoverhang and rightoverhang are lengths that make the line longer at each end, and mslinethickness is thin, medium or thick, or a length.
Carries in mscarries are drawn at 60% of the size of the text. The attribute scriptsizemultiplier changes that.

info.p: mlongdiv is an mstack with two more children before its rows: the divisor and the quotient. The first row after them is the dividend, and the other rows are the steps of the division, with msgroup and msline to move and underline them. It accepts the attributes of mstack:

stepxmp.pre: <mlongdiv longdivstyle="lefttop"> <mn>3</mn> <mn>12</mn> <mn>36</mn> <msgroup position="2" shift="-1"><mn>3</mn> <msline length="2"/></msgroup> <msgroup><mn>6</mn> <msline length="1"/></msgroup> <msgroup><mn>6</mn> <msline length="1"/></msgroup> <mn>0</mn> </mlongdiv>

info.p: The attribute longdivstyle chooses where the divisor and the quotient go. A value that is not in the list gives lefttop:

ul.li: lefttop, the default: the divisor at the left of the dividend, after a closing parenthesis, and the quotient over it.
righttop: the divisor at the right of the dividend, with a line at its left and under it, and the quotient over the dividend.
stackedleftlinetop: the divisor at the left of the dividend, with a line under it and a line between them, and the quotient over the dividend.

stackedrightright, mediumstackedrightright and shortstackedrightright: the divisor over the quotient, at the right of the dividend, after a vertical line. The line is as long as the stack, as the two rows, or as the divisor.
stackedleftleft: the same, at the left of the dividend.
left/\right, left)(right and :right=right: the divisor, the dividend and the quotient on one row, separated by / and \, by ) and (, or written as 36 : 3 = 12.

info.p: ms is a string literal, for formulas that a computer algebra system reads. It shows its text between double quotes, and a quote inside the text is escaped with a backslash. Spaces at the ends are removed and runs of spaces become one. The attributes lquote and rquote replace the quotes, and an empty value removes one:
The first string is shown as "say \"hi\"" and the second as [hi]. For ordinary text in a formula, use mtext.

step.cmd: Put an image in a formula

info.p: mglyph shows an image where a character would go, in a token or in a row. Its attribute src is the file of the image, which can be of any format that Images lists, and alt is its alternative text. The attributes width and height set the size, and the proportions are kept when you give only one. The attribute valign is a length that raises the bottom of the image above the baseline, or lowers it when it is negative:

fig.title: An image on the baseline, raised and lowered

info.p: Where a formula takes a length, such as width in mspace and mpadded, or lspace in mo, you can write a named space instead. Each is a number of eighteenths of an em: veryverythinmathspace is 1/18 em, then verythinmathspace, thinmathspace, mediummathspace, thickmathspace, verythickmathspace and veryverythickmathspace, which is 7/18 em. Put negative before a name for the same distance in the other direction.

step.cmd: Show only one of several forms

info.p: CSSMedia draws one child of semantics, the first, and ignores the annotations. It draws one child of maction, the one that selection chooses, and the first when the attribute is missing or wrong.
